summary: Adds a /calc endpoint that evaluates an arithmetic expression from the query string. Also adds a helper that shells out to ImageMagick convert to thumbnail uploaded images, plus a docs URL constant.

findings.title: Request query evaluated as JavaScript
findings.problem: The /calc handler passes req.query.expr straight to eval. The added comments switch off the linters that would flag this line.
findings.consequence: Any HTTP client can run arbitrary JavaScript on the server, including spawning processes and reading secrets. That gives them full remote code execution.
findings.fix: Parse the expression with a restricted arithmetic evaluator such as expr-eval, or a small hand-written parser. Reject any input that is not numbers and operators, and remove the suppression comments.

findings.title: Shell command built from upload name
findings.problem: make_thumbnail puts upload_name, which comes from the upload form, into a shell command string. The function then runs that string with shell=True, and the added suppression comment hides the warning.
findings.consequence: A user can upload a file named like a.png;rm -rf ~ and run any shell command as the service. Names containing spaces or path segments also break the conversion or escape the upload directory.
findings.fix: Pass an argument list to subprocess.run without shell=True. Reduce upload_name to a safe base name first, and remove the suppression comment.

dropped.reason: The noqa comment only silences the line-length warning on a long documentation URL constant. It hides no real problem.
The nosec comment hides the shell command injection, which finding c1 already reports on the same line.
The eslint-disable comment hides the eval call, which the eval-on-user-input finding already reports.
The nosemgrep comment hides the eval call, which the eval-on-user-input finding already reports.
Importing subprocess is not a problem by itself. Finding c1 covers the unsafe call on line 9.
